title: Model and Router contract (v1alpha1)
description: Machine-readable contract of a Model component and its Router specialization (F2-03). NON-NORMATIVE machine artifact: the normative source is spec/package/component-types.md §4-§5 and the spec/core/** documents it cites. A Model MUST be more than a name: it declares an input contract, an output contract, the capability contracts it satisfies, a resource contract (the shared hardware definition), an execution location, a service lifecycle when it runs as a service, a fallback, a version, a license and an artifact source. This contract MUST NOT reference the component descriptor: the model reuses the shared leaf definitions, so the composition edge component -> model-contract is one-way and the graph stays acyclic. Anchors: component-types.md §4.1-§4.9, §5.1-§5.4; core/requirements.md §2.4; core/distribution.md §3-§7.

input.description: Input contract of the model, expressed as an embedded JSON Schema. Whether this is an object, a string or a typed form is entirely OPEN (decision record §58, open question 'exact model-capability contract'): the internals are permissive and this schema MUST NOT fix a DSL or a capability grammar. The semantics that ARE fixed: the contract MUST describe the shape and the semantics of the model's input. F1: component-types.md §4.1.

output.description: Output contract of the model, expressed as an embedded JSON Schema, including typed outcomes where applicable. The internals are OPEN (decision record §58, open question 'exact model-capability contract') and MUST NOT be fixed at v1alpha1. The semantics that ARE fixed: the contract MUST describe the shape and the semantics of the model's output, including any typed outcomes. F1: component-types.md §4.2.

capabilities.description: The capability contracts this model satisfies, each expressed as a namespaced capability contract identifier, never as a hardcoded brand. A concrete implementation MAY be named only as a preferred or alternative implementation of a capability elsewhere and MUST NOT be required for conformance here. F1: component-types.md §4.1, §4.3.

resources.description: Resource contract of the model, reusing the single shared hardware definition (os, arch, cpu, ram, gpu, vram, disk) so the resource shape is never re-declared. F1: component-types.md §4.4; core/requirements.md §2.4.

executionLocation.description: Whether the model executes on the local machine or on a remote provider. Exactly two locations are recognized; a local model MUST NOT be presented as remote and vice versa. F1: component-types.md §4.5.

lifecycle.description: Service lifecycle of the model. The object is OPTIONAL overall: a model that does not run as a service declares none. When the model IS service-backed a lifecycle MUST be present, and all six actions (install, start, healthCheck, stop, update and remove) are REQUIRED, so the declaration always covers the full lifecycle. Each value is a human-readable descriptor of the action, not an executable command: executing a lifecycle action is owned by the Install Plan and Apply phases, which carry the corresponding risk class. F1: component-types.md §4.6, §10.1.

install.description: How the service is installed or bootstrapped. F1: component-types.md §10.1.

start.description: How the service is started. F1: component-types.md §10.1.

healthCheck.description: How the service health is checked. F1: component-types.md §10.1.

stop.description: How the service is stopped. F1: component-types.md §10.1.

update.description: How the service is updated. F1: component-types.md §10.1.

remove.description: How the service is removed. F1: component-types.md §10.1.

fallback.description: What happens when the model or its host is unavailable, including which decisions escalate to another capability. Fallback MUST be explicit; it MUST NOT be silent. F1: component-types.md §4.7.

version.description: Version of the model contract. MUST be valid Semantic Versioning 2.0.0. F1: component-types.md §4.8; core/versioning.md §2.

license.description: License of the model, an SPDX identifier where one exists. Whether a model license duplicates the package license declared once in the manifest metadata.license is OPEN (decision record §58, open question 'model license vs the single-declaration rule') and this schema MUST NOT decide that policy; the field is retained and left optional. F1: component-types.md §4.8; core/distribution.md §7.

artifactSource.description: Where the model artifact or provider is obtained. A concrete provider MUST NOT be fixed at v1alpha1: the provider is a free-form value and no vendor is hardcoded into the Core. F1: component-types.md §4.9; core/distribution.md §2, §4.

provider.description: Provider or source of the artifact. Deliberately NOT an enum and NOT a const: no provider is fixed, so the Core does not lock in a vendor. F1: component-types.md §4.9.

digest.description: Content digest of the model artifact, in the OCI form. A digest MUST always resolve to the same bytes. F1: core/distribution.md §4.

reference.description: Distribution reference of the artifact or provider. The reference MUST resolve to exactly one digest before Apply; the exact repository layout is deployment-specific. F1: core/distribution.md §2.

router.description: Optional Router specialization block. When present, the document is a Router: a Model specialization that routes, scores, gates or selects. F1: component-types.md §5.

Router-specific declaration. A Router MUST declare typed outputs and its thresholds and fallback behavior, including which decisions escalate to a generative capability, and MUST satisfy the Model declaration requirements in this same schema. A separate router schema is deliberately rejected so the Model and Router contracts stay in one place. F1: component-types.md §5.1-§5.4.

outputs.description: Typed outcomes the router can emit, for example a selected route, a score, or an abstention/no-op outcome. Typed outcomes are REQUIRED. F1: component-types.md §5.1.

thresholds.description: The thresholds the router applies. The concrete threshold grammar is OPEN (decision record §58, open question 'policy language / workflow graph'): this position is permissive and MUST NOT fix a threshold DSL. The semantics that ARE fixed: thresholds MUST be declared and MUST be inspectable. F1: component-types.md §5.2.

fallback.description: Router fallback behavior, including which decisions escalate to a generative capability. REQUIRED and MUST NOT be silent. F1: component-types.md §5.2.

escalation.description: Optional description of the escalation path from a router decision to a generative capability. F1: component-types.md §5.2.
